newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 28.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Wednesday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* Market is likely to see a brief correction phase due to the steep rise in stocks on Tuesday, traders said.

* "Prime candidates are issues whose prices have reached the upper limits of recent trading ranges. The release of first quarter GNP may also give investors an excuse to take profits," said BPI Securities Corp analyst Spencer Yap.

* Sun Hung Kai Securities Phil Inc said in its daily outlook that there may be spillover bargain hunting although there should be a close watch on foreign funds as their interest which was revived in Tuesday's session may be short-lived.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index posted its second biggest single-day rise for the year rising 112.71 points to close at 2,710.91.
* The Dow Jones on Tuesday ended 37.58 points higher to 7,383.41. PLDT's ADR rose $1 5/8 to $56 7/8.
* The Philippine peso closed higher at 26.374 to the dollar vs 26.375
* The Philippine interbank call loan average on Friday was at 18.0625 percent from 18.03125

* Mining firm Benguet Corp said it is optimistic that it will be able to reverse its losses in 1998 with new projects and after it secured a one-year moratorium on the principal payments of its 944 million pesos debts from 19 local and foreign banks early this year.
* PLDT had declared a 1.60 peso cash dividend for its common shareholders and a 50 centavo cash divided for its select preferred shareholders.

* Berjaya Lottery Management (HK) Ltd is taking the lead in restructuring Central Azucarera de Pilar under a swap arrangement, documents submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) showed.
* Philex Mining Corp said the SEC had approved the increase its authorised capital to five billion pesos from two billion.
* The benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate fell to an average of 10.892 percent at the regular auction on Tuesday from 11.166 percent last week, the Bureau of Treasury said.

* A Reuters poll of seven securities firms showed that a slowdown in the manufacturing sector and lower growth of overseas workers' remittances would cut GNP growth to 6.34 percent in the first quarter of the year from 6.6 a year earlier.
* The National Development Corp declared the bidding for its 7.5 percent stake in the National Steel Corp a failure because none put in any bids.
* The state-run National Power Corp's net income rose to 2.34 billion pesos in the first four months of the year from 1.73 billion a year earlier.

* Philippine Daily Inquirer reported that cities, towns and villages were mopping up on Tuesday after flash floods caused by a storm left 53 dead and 77,000 displaced in Metro Manila and in other places in the northern island of Luzon.
* BusinessWorld said that the Central Bank intends to further liberalise the registration requirements for portfolio investments coming in through commercial banks.

* Today and Inquirer said the SEC is considering the imposition of administrative sanctions against four brokerage firms implicated by a newspaper columnist in an alleged stock fraud involving more than seven million pesos worth of stock certificates and check payments.

* The Manila Times said a management audit report commissioned by one of the allegedly erring four brokerage firms revealed that the securities firm has committed numerous breaches of SEC and PSE rules including existence of dummy accounts, front running and filing of wrong reports.
* The Business Daily said the inter-agency Presidential Sugar Task Force rejected a last-ditch petition from the local sugar industry to retain current tariff protection for the sector.
